dek: A caller's trade idea for Bobby Witt Jr. split a group chat, so we ran the numbers.

slides.label: The Pitch
slides.text: A caller on The Michael Kay Show pitched it: send Cam Schlittler to Kansas City for *Bobby Witt Jr.*

slides.label: It Blew Up
slides.text: Yankees Worldwide posted the clip and it passed *94,000 plays* in a day. A group chat caught fire too.

slides.label: Cam's Resume
slides.text: Schlittler posted a *1.95 ERA*, 239 strikeouts and a *unanimous Cy Young*, the seventh Yankee ever.

slides.label: He Carried Them
slides.text: With Judge out nearly 100 games, Schlittler went 8-2 with a *1.16 ERA* on the road as the Yankees won 93.

slides.label: Witt's Case
slides.text: Witt hit .281 with 18 homers and 45 steals, an All-Star Evan called a *once in a lifetime* shortstop.

slides.label: The Fine Print
slides.text: Witt's *11 year, $288.7M* deal runs through 2034, with a *no-trade clause* giving him a say in any move.

slides.label: The Bar
slides.text: Danny's rule: Witt 'would have to put up a *50/40 season*' to be worth it. He's never hit 50 homers.

slides.label: The Verdict
slides.text: The group chat found common ground: Witt is a star, but *Cam is the ace* who held the season together.

The Cam Schlittler Bobby Witt Jr trade pitch blew up on social media this week, and we are not here for it. A caller on The Michael Kay Show floated sending our unanimous AL Cy Young winner to Kansas City for Bobby Witt Jr., and the clip passed 94,000 plays in a day.

Schlittler posted a 1.95 ERA and carried the Yankees to 93 wins while Aaron Judge missed nearly 100 games. Witt is a star, but his .800 OPS ranked 46th in baseball and his contract comes with a no-trade clause through 2034.

Our founder Danny Silverio and his friend Evan Sczerba argued it out in a group chat, and the numbers settled it.

caption_linkedin:
A fan pitched a trade this week: send Cam Schlittler, the Yankees' unanimous AL Cy Young winner, to Kansas City for Bobby Witt Jr. The clip went viral, and it is a good case study for anyone building a team, on the field or in a company.

Schlittler posted a 1.95 ERA and carried the Yankees to 93 wins while their MVP missed nearly 100 games. Witt is a great player, an All-Star with a long contract and a no-trade clause. But great is not the same as irreplaceable, and the numbers back that up. His .800 OPS ranked 46th in baseball this year.

Our founder and a lifelong fan argued it out in a group chat before the numbers settled it. The lesson holds outside baseball too. Know what you actually have before you trade it away for upside you have not proven.

Would you trade Schlittler for Witt Jr.?
